observation.visible_scene: A horizontal brass-colored cylindrical workpiece is clamped at the left in a metal lathe chuck (visible jaws top and bottom). A teal/blue band (tape-like ring) encircles the cylinder. A dark, pointed metal tool (cone/stylus shape) enters from the right and its tip rests on the cylinder surface at the right side of the blue band, near a small lifted flap at the band's edge. The background is dark and blurred.
visible_changes: The tool tip stays at or very near the cylinder surface across the whole clip, but its contact point moves: it begins near the upper boundary of the blue band at the right edge and ends lower and a bit further left across the band, wandering axially (rightward through the middle of the clip, then leftward toward the end).
Thin bright horizontal lines appear and become more distinct on the blue band as the clip progresses (one faint line early, two clearer lines late), located below the tool's contact point.
The chuck jaws at the top and bottom change orientation/shape from frame to frame, consistent with the held workpiece and chuck rotating about the horizontal axis.
The small triangular flap at the band's right edge persists throughout, with its outline/size looking slightly different over time.
The framing shifts only slightly; the blue band's left and right edges stay roughly fixed in the image, so most apparent motion is the tool and the rotating chuck rather than a large camera move.
outside_clip_unknowns: What the tool actually does to the surface (cutting, scribing, or merely marking) and whether the bright lines are cuts, scratches, or reflections.
Whether the chuck rotation is continuous or intermittent, and the rotation rate.
The state of the operation before t=0 and after t=3.2s (the segment is a temporal crop).
The identity of the blue band (adhesive tape vs. coating) and of the tool.
Any operator input driving the tool's path.
uncertain_details: Exact trajectory of the tool tip relative to the workpiece versus relative to the camera, since the blurred background gives weak camera-motion evidence.
Whether the axial 'rightward then leftward' drift of the tip is genuine tool motion or a small camera/workpiece shift.
Whether the lifted flap is being trimmed by the tool or is simply an unchanged feature.

trace.prompt:
Observe this actual video clip before reading any existing caption.
These are chronological samples of a TEMPORALLY CROPPED SEGMENT of a longer source video.
Both ends are arbitrary crop boundaries, not the beginning and completion of an action. Motion
may already be underway in the first view and may continue beyond the last. The endpoints need
NOT match or connect as a loop. Do not judge different endpoints as a physical inconsistency,
and do not invent a trigger, contact, start, stop, landing, disappearance or completion to make
the excerpt form a complete story. Missing context outside this segment stays unknown.
If an editing cut is visible inside the segment, distinguish it from continuous physical motion;
do not invent a smooth transition or a causal mechanism to connect the two views.
Describe what is visible during the excerpt, the actual changes, and supported persistent
properties. Cover the main visible process, not just scenery. Distinguish object movement from
camera movement, reflection from separate objects, expansion from translation, deformation from
occlusion, and an already ongoing process from its onset. Only state what the clip supports;
do not invent causes, an earlier impact, an unseen operator, material identities or later outcomes.
Do not infer motion from one frame, a visible seam or a single pose. Static intervals are valid.
Do not supply named physics laws. Compare each important entity's first and last image positions
and their relative positions before describing motion. Treat camera motion as uncertain when the
background evidence is insufficient, and retain clear relative changes despite that uncertainty.
Return JSON {"visible_scene":"...", "visible_changes":["observation supported within the excerpt"],
"outside_clip_unknowns":["unseen prerequisites or outcomes, only when relevant"],
"uncertain_details":["..."]}. Be concrete and concise, in English. This is not a complete event reconstruction.
